newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: ABS-CBN net up despite keener competition.
newsitem.headline: ABS-CBN net up despite keener competition.

text.p: ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp on Monday reported 22.35 percent growth in net income last year, and analysts said they expected it to maintain that pace this year despite keener competition among television networks.
ABS-CBN Broadcasting, the media subsidiary of holding company Benpres Holdings Corp, said its net income rose to 1.53 billion pesos ($58.17 million) in 1996 from 1.25 billion pesos the previous year.
Gross revenues reached 4.464 billion pesos, up 16.34 percent from 3.837 billion pesos.

"The network's financial results in 1996 again underscored our leadership in the local broadcasting industry, not only in terms of top-rating programmes and quality services but also in our financial stability," ABS-CBN senior vice-president Felipe Yalong said in a statement.
The growth pace was down from 1995, when net income grew 33.73 percent and gross revenues 28.76 percent.

Jonas Ferrer, research head of Pryce Securities, said income growth had been tempered by stiffer competition for advertising revenues and the company's aggressive expansion plan, which has increased its interest expense.
"These two factors have undermined its growth rate," Ferrer said. Nevertheless, he expected the company to register about 20 percent net income growth this year.
The company had alloted 500 million pesos to upgrade and expand its core business in 1997.
Spencer Yap, an analyst at BPI Securities, said contributions from its other business ventures would still keep the network's income healthy.
"Other businesses will start kicking in this year ... This is going to be a total entertainment company," he said.

Aside from its flagship television and radio operations, the company last year launched its first regional cable channel and an ultra-high frequency (UHF) channel, and built film theatres in key cities.
It also opened a retailing subsidiary to handle the marketing of specialty consumer products culled from its popular television shows.
"ABS-CBN will still be the dominant player in the industry. Its audience appeal is very strong," Yap added.
Jomar Lacson, an analyst at Philippine Asia Equity, said ABS-CBN's expansion programme would not affect its long-term viability since the diversification was well thought out.
Lacson said he expected the company to grow by more than 30 percent this year.
ABS-CBN is the country's biggest media company in terms of television and radio audiences and advertising revenues.
ABS-CBN closed 50 centavos higher on Monday at 31.50 pesos.
